    I am a PhD Student in Computer Science at the University of Milano-Bicocca, where my doctoral research explores Virtual Reality in mental healthcare at the intersection of artificial intelligence, physiological and environmental sensors, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), and serious games.
  
  
    Alongside my PhD, I have over four years of experience as a Software Developer and Research Technologist in the Digital Health Research unit at Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) in Trento, Italy. Working closely with clinicians and psychologists, I design and build interactive VR/XR applications, sensor-driven pipelines, and AI-assisted tools for applied healthcare research.

title: VR Reminiscence Therapy for Parkinson’s MCI
text:
Technical Contribution

Built the Unity VR application to immerse patients in familiar, personalised memory triggers.
Developed a companion tablet application allowing clinicians or facilitators to guide and control the VR experience during therapy sessions.
Implemented an image depth-visualisation pipeline to convert patients’ personal 2D photographs into immersive depth-enhanced visuals inside the virtual environment.

NotePhD Research Direction — University of Milano-Bicocca



My doctoral work in Computer Science investigates Virtual Reality in mental healthcare, bringing together AI, physiological and behavioural sensors, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), and serious games. As I am in the early stage of my PhD, I am currently refining my specific research question by building on applied clinical VR engineering experience at Fondazione Bruno Kessler.

title: iEMBRACE — Customised VR for Cognitive Decline
text:
Technical Contribution

Built a Unity VR application targeting the Meta Quest headset family for older adults experiencing cognitive decline and responsive behaviours.
Designed relaxing, interactive virtual environments supporting hand-gesture interaction so residents can engage naturally without complex controllers.
Developed a companion smartphone application enabling healthcare workers to supervise, customise, and control the VR session in real time.

title: Towards Shape-Aware Heart Rate Estimation
text:
Focus

Investigates shape-aware methods for heart rate estimation, bridging signal processing, geometric/morphological representations, and data-driven modelling.
Forms part of my broader technical background in integrating physiological sensors and AI-based tools for health-oriented interactive systems.
